m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll. (mfn.) eager, excited, impetuous; talking or discussing vehemently or excitedly; Ja II 422,13´ (~o nāma vippakiṇṇavāco); VI 521,24* (thiyo taṃ paribhāsiṃsu samāgantvā ~ā); Dhp-a I 330,.18 (janapadavāsino … kotūhalajātā); III 194,.11 (mahājano pi ~-jāto nikkhami); Dāṭh 5:22 (bhikkhū … kotūhalā sapadi sannipatiṃsu tattha); —      °-maṅgala,  kotūhalamaṅgala,   n., what is auspicious and portentous; special ceremonies and auspicious rites; A III 439,.18 (abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kotūhalamaṅgalena suddhiṃ paccāgantuṃ; Mp III 414,.7 : diṭṭhasutamutamaṅgalena); Ja I 373,.26 (kotūhalamaṅgalaṃ nām’ etaṃ na buddhapaccekabuddhabodhisattehi vaṇṇitaṃ); Nett 93,.13 (diṭṭhisampanno ~ena suddhiṃ pacceyyā ti n’ etaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati); — ifc see vata-; —       °(kotūhala)-maṅgalika,   mfn., trusting in omens and portents; setting store by ceremonies and auspicious rites; superstitious; A III 206,.8 (~o hoti, maṅgalaṃ pacceti no kammaṃ, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se kotuhala-; Mp III 302,.20 : ~o ti iminā idaṃ bhavissatī ti evaṃ pavattattā kotūhala-saṅkhātena diṭṭhasutamutamaṅgalena samannāgato); Ja I 373,.26 (na mayaṃ ~ā); — neg. akotūhalamaṅgalika, mfn., not superstitious; not trusting in omens and portents; A III 206,.17 (Be, Ce so; Ee, Se akotuhala-); —       °-sālā,  kotūhalasālā,   f.
